Subject: [PATCH] RDMA/bnxt_re: Avoid freeing MR resources if dereg fails

The driver returns an error code for MR dereg, but frees the MR structure.
When the MR dereg is retried due to previous error, the system crashes as
the structure is already freed.

Do not free the MR structures, when driver returns error to the stack.

Fixes: 872f3578241d ("RDMA/bnxt_re: Add support for MRs with Huge pages")
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/1574671174-5064-2-git-send-email-selvin.xavier@broadcom.com
Signed-off-by: Selvin Xavier <selvin.xavier@broadcom.com>
Signed-off-by: Jason Gunthorpe <jgg@mellanox.com>

diff --git a/drivers/infiniband/hw/bnxt_re/ib_verbs.c b/drivers/infiniband/hw/bnxt_re/ib_verbs.c
index 9b6ca15a183c..ad5112a2325f 100644
--- a/drivers/infiniband/hw/bnxt_re/ib_verbs.c
+++ b/drivers/infiniband/hw/bnxt_re/ib_verbs.c
@@ -3305,8 +3305,10 @@ int bnxt_re_dereg_mr(struct ib_mr *ib_mr, struct ib_udata *udata)
 	int rc;
 
 	rc = bnxt_qplib_free_mrw(&rdev->qplib_res, &mr->qplib_mr);
-	if (rc)
+	if (rc) {
 		dev_err(rdev_to_dev(rdev), "Dereg MR failed: %#x\n", rc);
+		return rc;
+	}
 
 	if (mr->pages) {
 		rc = bnxt_qplib_free_fast_reg_page_list(&rdev->qplib_res,

2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/infiniband/hw/bnxt_re/ib_verbs.c`**
   - **Line Changes:**
     - The code block that handles the deregistration of memory regions (MR) has been modified. Specifically, the check for the return code (`rc`) from the function `bnxt_qplib_free_mrw` has been updated.
     - If `rc` indicates an error (i.e., if `rc` is non-zero), the error message is logged using `dev_err`, and the function now returns the error code immediately without proceeding to free the MR structure.
     - This prevents the MR structure from being freed if the deregistration fails, addressing the issue that could lead to a kernel crash.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `ib_verbs.c` directly addresses the bug described in the patch. The original code incorrectly freed the MR structure even when deregistration failed, which could lead to a NULL pointer dereference if the deregistration was retried. By ensuring that the MR structure is not freed when an error occurs, the patch prevents potential crashes and maintains the integrity of the memory management within the driver.
- The patch is linked to a previous commit (identified by the hash `872f3578241d`), which introduced support for MRs with huge pages. The fix is necessary to correct the behavior introduced in that commit, ensuring that the driver handles error conditions appropriately without leading to system instability.

Do not free the MR structures, when driver returns error to the stack.

Fixes: 872f3578241d ("RDMA/bnxt_re: Add support for MRs with Huge pages")
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/1574671174-5064-2-git-send-email-selvin.xavier@broadcom.com
Signed-off-by: Selvin Xavier <selvin.xavier@broadcom.com>
Signed-off-by: Jason Gunthorpe <jgg@mellanox.com>

Here is the root cause:
The bug is caused by freeing the Memory Region (MR) structure even when the deregistration process returns an error code. This leads to the MR structure being accessed after it has been freed, which can result in a kernel NULL pointer dereference when attempts are made to retry deregistration. The failure to handle error codes properly during the deregistration process creates a situation where the system can crash if the same MR is attempted to be deregistered multiple times.

Here is the patch:
 
 int bnxt_re_dereg_mr(struct ib_mr *ib_mr, struct ib_udata *udata)
 {
 	struct bnxt_re_mr *mr = container_of(ib_mr, struct bnxt_re_mr, ib_mr);
 	struct bnxt_re_dev *rdev = mr->rdev;
 	int rc;
 
 	rc = bnxt_qplib_free_mrw(&rdev->qplib_res, &mr->qplib_mr);
-	if (rc)
+	if (rc) {
 		dev_err(rdev_to_dev(rdev), "Dereg MR failed: %#x\n", rc);
+		return rc;
+	}
 
 	if (mr->pages) {
 		rc = bnxt_qplib_free_fast_reg_page_list(&rdev->qplib_res,
 							&mr->qplib_frpl);
 		kfree(mr->pages);
 		mr->npages = 0;
 		mr->pages = NULL;
 	}
 	ib_umem_release(mr->ib_umem);
 
 	kfree(mr);
 	atomic_dec(&rdev->mr_count);
 	return rc;
 }
